sources.entry: AI Context Templates - Free CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, and PRP templates that make AI coding assistants actually useful. 5 ready-to-use template packs for common project types.

summary.one_liner: A set of free, fill-in-the-blank context templates (CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, and PRP prompts) meant to help AI coding assistants follow a project's conventions, with a paid premium bundle of deeper packs.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents three free templates: a CLAUDE.md starter for project context, a basic .cursorrules template, and a PRP (prompt) feature template. Each is a markdown file to fill in with project specifics and drop into a repository root so the assistant reads it at the start of a session. The README describes a premium bundle at $19 with extra packs: multiple .cursor/rules/*.mdc files with glob-based activation, PRP templates for features, bug fixes, refactors and integrations, a multi-agent config pack, an AGENTS.md template, and an expanded CLAUDE.md covering architecture, testing, gotchas and CI/CD. The README contains no code, scripts, or installation process; it is primarily guidance and template text. A live landing page is linked but no details are given beyond the title.
use_cases: Writing a CLAUDE.md project context file for Claude Code
Setting up a .cursorrules file for Cursor
Getting AI assistants to match existing code style and naming
Drafting a feature prompt (PRP) with clear requirements
Reducing time spent correcting AI-generated code
Configuring rules for glob-based file-type activation (premium)
how_to_run: Pick the template matching your tool (CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, or PRP).
Fill in the [bracketed] placeholders with your project specifics.
Delete sections that do not apply.
Drop the file into your repository root.
notable: Free CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, and PRP starter templates with explained sections
Covers both Claude Code and Cursor conventions in one repo
Premium tier adds glob-scoped .mdc rules for API routes, database files, and tests
Templates are plain markdown with [bracket] placeholders to customize
Includes a PRP template aimed at first-try feature prompts
caveats: The premium bundle is paid ($19) and its purchase link is not yet live per the README
README contains no installation, tooling, or automation; it is template text and guidance only
Claims such as 90%+ first-try accuracy and the 57% enterprise statistic are not backed by data in the repo
